{{Use British English|date=March 2017}}
'''Peter Comrie''' [[FRSE]] LLD EIS (1868 – 1944) was a Scottish mathematician and educator. He served as Rector of [[Leith Academy]] 1922 to 1933 and President of the Edinburgh Mathematical Society 1916–17.

==Life==
He was born on 17 July 1868 in [[Muthill]] the son of Peter Comrie, master blacksmith and Elizabeth Ritchie.<ref name="st-and">{{cite web|url=http://www-history.mcs.st-and.ac.uk/Biographies/Comrie.html|website=History.mcs.st-and.ac.uk|title=Comrie biography|access-date=10 April 2018}}</ref>
He was educated at [[Muthill]] School and then [[Morrison's Academy]] in [[Crieff]]. He then won a place at [[St Andrews University]] studying Mathematics, graduating BSc, MA.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.royalsoced.org.uk/cms/files/fellows/biographical_index/fells_indexp1.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=29 October 2015 |archive-date=24 January 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130124115814/http://www.royalsoced.org.uk/cms/files/fellows/biographical_index/fells_indexp1.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>
From 1895 he began working as a mathematics teacher, firstly in [[Greenock Academy]], then [[Hutcheson's Grammar School]], and [[Robert Gordon's College]]. In 1904 he moved to [[Edinburgh]] and remained there for the rest of his life, but teaching in various schools. Firstly in [[Boroughmuir High School]] then in 1917 received his first role as headmaster: at Castlehill School at the head of the [[Royal Mile]]. In 1922 he moved to be headmaster of [[Leith Academy]] where he remained until retiral in 1933.<ref name="auto">''[[The Scotsman]]'': 22 December 1944</ref>

He was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]] in 1909 his main proposer being [[James Donaldson (classical scholar)|Sir James Donaldson]].
[[St Andrews University]] awarded him an honorary doctorate (LLD) in 1928.

He died at home 19 Craighouse Terrace in [[Edinburgh]] on 20 December 1944.<ref name="auto"/>

==Memberships==
*President of the Edinburgh Mathematical Society (1916 and 1917)
*President of the Educational Institute of Scotland (1928)
*Co-opted member of the Education Committee for Edinburgh Corporation (1933–44)
*Governor of [[George Heriot's School|George Heriot's Trust]]
*Member of the Edinburgh Provincial Committee
*Member of the Central Executive Committee for Training of Teachers (in Scotland)

==Publications==
*''Chambers New Commercial Arithmetic'' (1911)

==Family==
Comrie was married to Charlotte Aikman from St Andrews.<ref name="st-and2">{{cite web|url=http://www-groups.dcs.st-and.ac.uk/history/Obits2/Comrie_obituary.html|website=Groups.dcs.st-and.ac.uk|title=EMS obituary|access-date=10 April 2018}}</ref>
